corrections: Split seven long lessons into 38 units with stable distinct IDs, sourceLesson, honest 3–5-minute values, ordered migrations, unit-specific takeaways, and independent focused question files.

Preserved all fourteen archival MD/question files byte for byte and all 84 original question IDs, type, level, answer keys and option counts; no new question was required because every unit had at least one suitable original question.

Added explanatory code comments for field extraction, byte order, fragment alignment/offset units, reverse mappings, route matching, settled-node skipping, path relaxation, tuple ranking, DHCP option bounds/concatenation and timer output. Original native executable statements remain identical; one added ipaddress import makes the split aggregation snippet standalone.
Corrected RFC 6691 advertised-MSS versus actual-payload wording: the advertisement subtracts fixed headers without options; a sender separately reduces its actual data length for included options.

Made the sequential IPv4 Identification wrap calculation dimensionally explicit, including grouped rate denominators and every unit. Used conventional implicit algebra in products and bracketed compound expressions.

Added local prerequisite context for Python strict network parsing, documentation-only NAT64 suffix encoding, and source-specific Linux reply routing so each moved question is answerable before completion of its own unit.

Qualified the 4-to-3 modulo ECMP example with uniform-hash, removed-last-path and stable-surviving-index assumptions; removed the overstatement that changing the path count changes almost every remainder in general.

Audited every inherited glossary definition, alias and example. Corrected/qualified 180 inherited entries and retained all 430 IDs, adding three precise local terms. Review groups overlap; 180 is an entry count, not an atomic-fact claim count.

Significant glossary repairs include NAT mapping versus filtering, no inherent VPN encryption, IP scope versus actual reachability, /31 limited-broadcast distinction, non-atomic Identification semantics, OSPF flooding/adjacency/area summaries, source preference, non-universal route withdrawal, no TLS plaintext guarantee from rogue DHCP, DAD/ARP non-guarantees, and DHCP timing/configuration qualifications.
Corrected the DHCP magic-cookie definition: BOOTP can use the same RFC 1048-style cookie, so its presence alone does not distinguish DHCP from every BOOTP message.

Removed stale prevalence/default/timing guarantees from inherited examples (Linux majority, fixed keepalive interval, universal MAC rotation, guaranteed direct NAT traversal, universal SPF per event, always-fatal malformed BGP UPDATE, global ROA coverage). Replaced a provider-specific community number with an explicitly hypothetical agreed tag.

Checked the real compiled IDs, full definitions and rendered links.

glossary nat66 (new): definition/example implied NPTv6 could substitute for a larger delegation; RFC 6296 NPTv6 is stateless and 1:1 (Abstract, §3.7), so it cannot fit more internal subnets into a smaller external prefix → definition rewritten (stateless 1:1 NPTv6 vs stateful port-translating forms) and example changed to RFC 6296's provider-independence use.

ip-nat-ipv6-q4 option C explanation said IPv6-to-IPv6 translation 'can be made to work in some designs' for three subnets in one /64 → now states that NPTv6 maps addresses 1:1 and cannot, and only stateful port-translating NAT66 could, at NAT's usual cost.

ip-ipv4-path-mtu analogy: the bridge keeper 'turns it back', implying an oversized DF packet returns to the sender → the lorry is stopped (dropped), only the note (ICMP) returns, and any resend comes from the sender's transport; also removed 'posted', which opened the HTTP POST entry.

ip-subnet-worked-ranges.rationale: Reviewed: A short inline 'rulers laid end to end' image suffices; the prefix-mask lesson carries the callout. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-subnet-vlsm-plan.rationale: Reviewed: Allocation table and worked examples are the mental model; prefix-mask lesson already has the address analogy. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-subnet-special-ranges.rationale: Reviewed: A reference list of reserved ranges; an analogy would not add understanding. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-subnet-route-aggregation.rationale: Verified: Telephone area codes map aggregate prefixes and detailed routes held at the summarising router; limit: unassigned numbers still attract calls, and prefixes need power-of-two alignment.

ip-nat-port-mappings.rationale: Verified: Office switchboard maps public number/lines/extensions to address/ports/mappings and static forwards; limit covers packet rewriting, idle expiry and filtering.

ip-nat-traversal-connectivity.rationale: Verified: Two callers behind switchboards map STUN, signalling, hole punching, TURN and ICE; limit covers destination-dependent mapping and paced parallel checks.

ip-ipv6-address-notation.rationale: Reviewed: Notation rules and type table are procedural. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-ipv6-slaac-identifiers.rationale: Reviewed: Procedural steps and privacy consequence are concrete; no analogy added. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-ipv6-transition-paths.rationale: Reviewed: The step-by-step walkthrough is the model; the NAT switchboard analogy already covers translation state. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-routing-longest-prefix.rationale: Verified: Mail-sorting rulebook maps rule precision to prefix length and the default; limit: binary prefixes and next hop only. Verifier removed place names that opened wrong dictionary entries; mapping unchanged.

ip-routing-selection-rib-fib.rationale: Reviewed: Two-stage selection is shown directly by the questions' scenarios. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-routing-per-hop.rationale: Verified: Parcel label versus per-leg courier sticker maps IP header versus Ethernet frame; limit notes TTL/checksum changes, NAT/tunnels and non-Ethernet links.

ip-routing-trie-tcam.rationale: Reviewed: Trie diagram and TCAM ordering scenario are already concrete. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-routing-ecmp-asymmetry.rationale: Verified: Checkout lanes by surname map flows, hashing, affinity and modulo churn; limit covers elephant flows and resilient hashing. Verifier softened 'most families' to 'many' and 'avoids' to 'reduces' reordering.

ip-igp-distance-vector.rationale: Verified: Village signposts map distance-vector tables and neighbour updates; limit introduces stale beliefs and count to infinity.

ip-igp-count-to-infinity.rationale: Reviewed: Trace table already concrete; distance-vector lesson's signpost analogy foreshadows it. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-ospf-neighbours-lsdb.rationale: Verified: Shared road atlas maps LSAs, flooding, LSDB and per-router SPF; limit covers transient inconsistency and area scope.

ip-ospf-interface-costs.rationale: Reviewed: The table and trap warning are concrete. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-ospf-worked-spf.rationale: Reviewed: The trace table is the mental model. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-ospf-areas-designated.rationale: Verified: Meeting chair and deputy map DR/BDR, Two-Way and non-pre-emptive election; limit: the DR does not relay data traffic. Verifier reworded 'the segment' so it opens shared-segment rather than TCP segment.

ip-bgp-as-paths.rationale: Verified: Courier handling slips map AS_PATH, loop rejection and path-length preference; limit: unsigned claims and prepending.

ip-bgp-sessions-reflectors.rationale: Reviewed: R1/R2/R3 example is concrete; AS_PATH analogy precedes it. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-bgp-best-path.rationale: Verified: Preferred suppliers map LOCAL_PREF before AS_PATH length and prepending; limit: no performance measurement, fixed vendor order.

ip-bgp-commercial-policy.rationale: Reviewed: The business relationships are themselves the familiar framing. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-bgp-routing-incidents.rationale: Reviewed: Real incidents serve as concrete examples. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-bgp-rpki-validation.rationale: Verified: Signed collection authorisation maps ROA, origin AS, maxLength and local drop policy; limit: only the final name is checked, NotFound passes.

ip-dhcp-discovery-dora.rationale: Reviewed: The four-message sequence diagram is already the model. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-dhcp-message-options.rationale: Reviewed: Byte-level TLV parsing is clearer as code. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-dhcp-lease-timers.rationale: Verified: Library loan maps lease, renewal at T1, rebinding at T2 and expiry; limit: no penalty, server policy and address reuse.

ip-dhcp-relays-security.rationale: Reviewed: Relay diagram and trusted/untrusted ports are concrete. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.

ip-dhcp-join-troubleshoot.rationale: Reviewed: End-to-end trace is itself the integrating example. The visible explanation and questions need no comparison.
